about: F658 (A86): which respawn station a down player's phone uses. One rule, two readers: app/src/beacon.js (Presence and respawnStation, read by engine.js) through app/test/respawn-station-cases.test.mjs, and the stage's twin in mcp/brx_mcp/stage/stage.py through mcp/tests/test_respawn_station_cases.py. The phone decides whether a station is enabled: only a station that the player's own config.stations lists with kind respawn. Its game byte does not matter, so a station set up for an earlier game keeps working with no re-arm. `config_stations` is the bundle's list (null = absent). `player` is the gun's team tid and the game bytes it plays in turn, on one presence tracker. `heard` lists the station adverts heard in each of those games (`present` is the presence verdict). `expect` is the station id used in every game (null = none); `expect_heard`, when given, the station ids the tracker keeps in every game.

cases.name: a respawn station the match config does not list is ignored
an id listed with another kind does not enable a respawn station
no config.stations: no respawn station is in play
a listed station that advertises another game byte still works
a station armed for an old game keeps working in every later game with no re-arm
team scoping holds: another team's station is never mine, a neutral one admits every team
a present station comes before a stronger one that is not present
a disabled station (state 0) is never used
only respawn adverts ignore the game byte: a control point or a powerup of another game is still dropped
a station on game 0 (any) and a player on game 0 both still work
